config.title: CEDT Grader
config.displayLanguage.description: Language of the CEDT Grader panel, statement viewer, messages and status bar. Changes apply at once. Command names, settings and the walkthrough follow VS Code's own display language. Grader content (problem names, compiler messages) is never translated.
config.displayLanguage.enum.auto: The language VS Code is displayed in (Thai if VS Code is in Thai, otherwise English)
config.panel.sections.description: Sections of the CEDT Grader panel, in the order shown. Remove one to hide it; reorder the list to move them. **Account** always comes back while you are logged out (it holds the login form). Empty = all sections.
config.panel.sections.current: Current problem: the open file's problem, counted score, language and Submit
config.panel.sections.result: Result: the latest submission's verdict per test
config.panel.sections.history: History: every submission for the problem
config.panel.sections.problems: Problems: all problems with their counted score
config.panel.compact.description: Compact panel: tighter spacing, the counted score on one line, one-line problem rows (full name in the tooltip) and smaller verdict tiles.
config.panel.topicClickOrder.description: What a click on a topic pill in the Problems list does first. Each click moves to the next state; the third click turns the topic filter off again.
config.panel.topicClickOrder.showFirst: First click shows only problems with that topic, the second hides them, the third turns it off.
config.panel.topicClickOrder.hideFirst: First click hides problems with that topic, the second shows only them, the third turns it off.
config.baseUrl.description: Base URL of the cafe-grader-web server. Read from user settings only (a workspace cannot change where your password is sent).
config.username.description: Your grader login name. The password is stored in the OS keychain (VS Code SecretStorage), never in settings.
config.pollIntervalSeconds.description: Seconds between status checks while a submission is graded (minimum 3). Polling only runs right after a submission and stops after 3 minutes.
config.confirmBeforeSubmit.description: Ask once before submitting a file whose problem was matched automatically (by file name, folder name or CPH data). Submitting saves the match as your choice, so it isn't asked again. Problems you chose yourself are never asked; suggestions always are.
config.saveBeforeSubmit.description: Save the file before submitting, so the grader gets exactly what is on disk. Save actions such as format on save run first. Turn off to submit the editor's text without saving.
config.revealResultAfterSubmit.descripti: When grading finishes, open the **Result** section in the panel and scroll it into view. Keyboard focus stays in your editor.
config.debugRequests.description: Log every grader request (method, path, status) and cache hit/miss to the **CEDT Grader: Requests** output channel, to check request counts. Never logs passwords or tokens.
config.statementBeside.description: Open problem statements in an editor tab beside your code.
config.statementFollowsFile.description: An open statement tab switches to the problem of the file you switch to, and closes when that source file has no problem.
config.defaultLanguage.description: Language for "New file for this problem" when the active file's language isn't allowed and no language was used before (e.g. C++, Python, Java). Archive and other non-source languages are never chosen automatically.
config.fileNamePattern.description: File name for **New file for this problem** and **Rename file to match the problem**. `{name}` = the problem name, `{id}` = the problem id, `{ext}` = the language's extension; must end with `.{ext}`. Files named this way are also matched to their problem automatically. Example: `{id}_{name}.{ext}` → `1360_00_Intro_11.cpp`.
config.cacheMaxMB.description: Size limit (MB) for downloaded problem statements and test cases. When it is exceeded, the least recently used files are deleted first. Files unused for 30 days are removed automatically. Use **CEDT Grader: Clear Cached Data…** to clear everything.
walkthrough.title: Get started with CEDT Grader
walkthrough.description: Log in, link a solution file to its problem and submit it, without leaving VS Code.
walkthrough.openPanel.title: Open the CEDT Grader panel
walkthrough.openPanel.description:
Everything happens in the **CEDT Grader** panel: the page-with-a-check-mark icon in the left bar.
[Open the Panel](command:cedtGrader.focus)
walkthrough.login.title: Log in
walkthrough.login.description:
Use your grader username and password. Leave **Remember password on this computer** on if this is your own computer.
[Log In](command:cedtGrader.login)
walkthrough.openFile.title: Open a solution file
walkthrough.openFile.description:
Open the folder with your solutions, then a solution file such as `00_Intro_11.cpp`.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)
walkthrough.checkProblem.title: Check the problem
walkthrough.checkProblem.description:
A file named like a problem is linked to it automatically. Otherwise choose the problem under **Current problem**; your choice is remembered.
[Choose Problem](command:cedtGrader.chooseProblem)
walkthrough.submit.title: Submit
walkthrough.submit.description:
Press **Submit to Grader** in the panel. The verdict of every test and your counted score appear when grading is done.
[Submit Current File](command:cedtGrader.submit)
walkthrough.cph.title: Optional: install CPH
walkthrough.cph.description:
Competitive Programming Helper runs test cases on your computer. With it, **Load test cases** puts the grader's test cases into CPH. Everything else works without it.
[Show CPH](command:extension.open?%5B%22DivyanshuAgrawal.competitive-programming-helper%22%5D)
